competitive_landscape: Frioul–If Express (RTM-operated) covers the harbour shuttle; TLV-TVM operates the seasonal Îles d'Hyères ferries from Tour Fondue and Le Lavandou. Calanques access is dominated by Cassis-based diesel day-tripper boats. Nothing on the corridor operates an electric or foiling tier. The regulatory regime around Calanques and Port-Cros actively favours a quiet-mode entrant.

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: Pioneer II covers the entire corridor — Vieux-Port↔Frioul (~2 nm), Marseille↔Cassis (~12 nm), Toulon↔Porquerolles (~10 nm), Marseille↔Porquerolles (~40 nm) — all inside the 70 nm all-electric envelope on year-round Mediterranean lee water.
navier_fit.quanta_lr: Hybrid Quanta-LR adds the Riviera and Corsica extenders — Marseille↔Calvi (~140 nm), Marseille↔Nice (~95 nm) — and the longer Pelagos-Sanctuary transit corridors with no charging-infrastructure dependency.

precedents.why_it_matters: Îles d'Hyères sit ~30 nm from St-Tropez (built cote-dazur-france). Treat as 'extend the Riviera eastward' rather than a standalone — keeps network coherence.

regulatory_note: Med SOx-ECA + FuelEU Maritime apply across the whole corridor. Calanques NP runs an active visitor-cap and access-permit regime (Sugiton, En Vau). Port-Cros is France's / Europe's first marine national park (1963) with strict wake and anchoring controls. The Pelagos Sanctuary for cetaceans overlays the whole offshore zone. France's national MPA framework is among the most aggressive enforcers in the Western Med — quiet-mode foiling is a near-perfect fit.
seasonality: Peak July–August for Calanques and Îles d'Hyères; shoulder months (May–June, September–October) are the sweet spot under the Calanques visitor-cap regime. Frioul commuter base is year-round. The corridor is sheltered behind Cap Sicié and the Hyères peninsula; only true open-Med Quanta legs (Calvi, Corsica) see genuine winter exposure.

summary: France's largest port and second city anchors a mixed urban-commuter and protected-nature corridor: the Frioul islands off Marseille, the Calanques National Park (overtourism-capped, 2–3M visitors), and the Îles d'Hyères — Porquerolles and Port-Cros — about 40 nm east. The standout is the regulatory / quiet-mode stack: Port-Cros was France's (and Europe's) first marine national park (1963), Calanques is a national park, and the western edge of the Pelagos Sanctuary for cetaceans overlays the whole corridor on top of the Med SOx-ECA. The Îles d'Hyères sub-cluster sits ~30 nm from St-Tropez (built Côte d'Azur) — close enough to extend the Riviera node eastward.
tagline: Europe's first marine national park (Port-Cros, 1963) overlaid with the Calanques NP — a textbook quiet-mode regulatory stack.
